sections.name: File setup, clean, quotations
sections.title: Setup and quotation rules
sections.what: Reads the wind report and the retrieval list, parses the report, and sets the rule for which quotations count: exact text of at least 18 characters with no ellipsis, after removing escape slashes.
sections.why: The code comment says ellipsized paraphrases must never be joined into verbatim text, which is why such quotes are dropped.
sections.watch_out: Short quotations are silently ignored, so a fact supported only by a short quote will show no evidence.

sections.name: evidence (part 1)
sections.title: Collecting evidence from the uploaded report
sections.what: Goes through every wind project and records each claim from the uploaded report as evidence. For each claim it also looks up the cited original web pages and keeps a quote only if that exact wording appears there. It then builds each project's list of participants, each tied to the claims that support it.
sections.why: The code comment says to quote only the claim's own cell so that neighboring money or status cells are not pulled in. The rest of the reason is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The participant step stops the whole script with an error if a listed role has no supporting claim, so one missing label can block the entire run.

sections.name: evidence (part 2)
sections.title: Adding primary package research quotes
sections.what: Adds a small set of extra quotes from primary documents to matching projects, each accepted only if its exact wording is found on the cited page. It also attaches a fixed construction statement from an NKT press release to East Anglia Three as the source for that project's stage and status. If that check fails, the script stops.
sections.why: The code comments say a forecast alone is not evidence of construction, and that primary research only adds to a dossier. The reason for the fixed statement beyond that is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The East Anglia quote, its date and the project key are typed in by hand, so a changed source page or renamed project will stop the script.

sections.name: uniqueEvidence
sections.title: Removing duplicate evidence rows
sections.what: Keeps one evidence row for each combination of project, field, web address and quoted text. It also marks references that share an exact web address as aliases of each other, and relabels references that point to a project's own admitted document.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same quote can be found through several routes, and one row per quote keeps the output clean. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The relabeling depends on the exact text beginning with the word Admitted, so changing that wording elsewhere would quietly stop the relabeling.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Writing the prepared output file
sections.what: Packages the projects, references, evidence and report details into one object, with a fingerprint of the report file and the full raw report text, and saves it as a JSON file in the wind ingest folder. It then prints a short count summary of projects, claims, references and verified quotes to the console.
sections.why: The fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) of the report lets later steps confirm which report produced the file. The reason for storing the raw text is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Each run overwrites the existing prepared.json with no backup, so keep a copy if the previous output matters.
